content.value_statement: Creating reliable plugin agents is difficult when triggers, tools, and prompts are unclear. This skill provides reusable patterns for agent structure, validation, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains required agent frontmatter fields and validation rules.
Provides templates for trigger descriptions with examples and commentary.
Shows how to structure agent system prompts for autonomous work.
Recommends tool scopes for analysis, code generation, and testing agents.
Includes complete examples for review, testing, documentation, and security agents.
Includes a local script for validating agent markdown files.
limitations: It is focused on Claude Code plugin agents, not general chatbot design.
It does not automatically install or publish agents.
The validation script checks structure, not runtime behavior quality.
Generated agents still need project-specific testing before use.

use_cases.title: Create a New Plugin Agent
use_cases.description: Design an agent with a valid identifier, trigger examples, model choice, color, tools, and system prompt.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Triggering
use_cases.description: Rewrite vague descriptions into precise trigger conditions with examples that show when the agent should run.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Safety Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether an agent uses least-privilege tools and has clear responsibilities, output format, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single-purpose agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code plugin agent for [task]. Include the identifier, trigger description, model, color, tool scope, and system prompt outline.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Triggering Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve when an agent should be used.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description for trigger quality: [description]. Make it specific, add examples, and explain when not to use the agent.

prompt_templates.title: Design Least-Privilege Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose safe tools for an agent role.
prompt_templates.prompt: For an agent that handles [responsibilities], recommend the minimum Claude Code tools it needs. Explain each tool choice and any tool to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Agent Plugin
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of several agents in one plugin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these planned agents: [agent list]. Check naming, trigger overlap, tool scope, model choice, prompt structure, and validation gaps.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews pull requests for code quality.
output_examples.output: A reviewer agent plan with a clear identifier, trigger examples for pull requests, read-only tools, quality checks, and a structured report format.

output_examples.input: Improve this agent description so it triggers more reliably.
output_examples.output: A revised trigger description with concrete examples, commentary for each example, exclusions, and wording that avoids broad activation.

output_examples.input: Check whether my testing agent has the right tool permissions.
output_examples.output: A tool-scope recommendation that explains required read and search access, when shell access is useful, and which permissions are unnecessary.

best_practices: Write trigger descriptions with concrete user requests and clear commentary.
Give each agent only the tools required for its responsibilities.
Validate the agent file and test realistic triggering scenarios before publishing.
anti_patterns: Using generic names or broad descriptions that trigger on unrelated tasks.
Granting full tool access when read-only tools are enough.
Shipping agents without output expectations, edge cases, or validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code plugin agents with frontmatter, trigger examples, system prompts, and validation guidance.

faq.question: Does it generate complete agent files?
faq.answer: It provides templates and examples that guide complete agent creation. You still choose the final task, tools, and wording.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to draft, review, and improve Claude Code agent files.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes an optional validation script, but the documentation does not require automatic command execution.

faq.question: How should I choose tools for an agent?
faq.answer: Start with the smallest useful tool set. Add write or shell access only when the agent role clearly requires it.

faq.question: What should I test before publishing an agent?
faq.answer: Test trigger examples, non-trigger examples, output format, tool boundaries, and edge cases in realistic project scenarios.
